verdict.rationale: Rootly documents retrospective templates with AI blocks that draft sections such as Curated Timeline from the incident's timeline, Slack and transcripts. It also provides a collaborative editor and configurable step-by-step retrospective processes routed by severity, which imply a review stage. A formal review/approval step and a publication step are not explicitly documented; the only distribution path shown is exporting to an external editor. Missing for 10: explicit review/approval workflow, a documented publish/share step, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, postmortems follow a real workflow — templates, drafting from the timeline, review, and publication

citations.quote: You decide which blocks belong in a retrospective by adding them to a template, and every retrospective created from that template generates those sections automatically.
sections like Summary, Impact, Root Cause, Mitigation, Resolution, and Curated Timeline get drafted automatically from the incident's data, Slack channel, and bridge-call transcripts
Right-size retrospective processes by severity, type, or team; auto-draft with Rootly AI; and drive follow-ups through configurable step-by-step processes.
so a SEV0 gets full formal treatment while a SEV3 gets a lightweight review.
Rootly includes a rich text editor in retrospectives that supports live incident data and real-time collaboration - all without leaving the platform.
Many teams use a hybrid approach by drafting in the Rootly document editor and exporting a copy to their external editor of choice.
